Question 6
?

(x−2y)6=

a
x6+12x5y+1024x4y2+…
b
x6+12x5y+30x4y2+…
c
x6−12x5y+24x4y2+…
d
x6−12x5y+80x4y2+…
e
x6−12x5y+60x4y2+…
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer n, we have

(a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

In the case of (x−2y)6, we have a=x, b=−2y, n=6.

Therefore, the first three terms of (x−2y)6 are as follows:

(x−2y)6=(60)(x)6(−2y)0+(61)(x)6−1(−2y)1+(62)(x)6−2(−2y)2+…=1(x)6+6(x)5(−2y)+15(x)4(4y2)+…=x6−12x5y+60x4y2+…
